done.why: I got the amulet, the cloak and hood, the vial and the sword, and by turn 104 the score said 'potential 3 of a possible 7'. After that every exit I hadn't tried said 'Not today' or turned me back. That was the mist west of the Barren Area, the rockslide to the northwest, the beach path north, the squeeze east of the Creepy Crawl, the rockfall east of the Junction, and the south and west shores of the lake. The stair is endless and the ship won't come back. I couldn't find another thread to pull, so I left.

about: An old wizard is testing you in a ruined underground realm. You have to prove yourself worthy by doing the right thing, not the violent thing. You call to a passing sailor, dive for an amulet, and beat a hooded double without killing it, and under the hood you find your own face. The place is a small, closed circle of the shadow land, the sea and a cold lake. Everything past that is walled off, gently but for good.

moments.note: 'Who do you think you are? Arthur?' Funny refusal for the sword in the rock.
West into the vegetation: the mist turns me back. It was the first of many blocked ways.
After waiting, a Viking ship passed with a sailor cupping his ear. Saying 'hello sailor' got me a gift. Very satisfying.
The hooded figure appeared, the sword from the junction jumped into my hand, and then the figure vanished when I moved.
A second grab in the sand got the golden amulet, and I came up wearing it.
After the fight I took the hood instead of killing, and saw my own weary face turn into an old man's. A strong moment.
Jumping in the lake made me drop everything, including things I was wearing. The shore warned me about the light, but I didn't think worn things counted.
I swam south, got turned back, and the roc ate me. I woke in the wizard's prison cell vision and then back at the stair, with my things scattered (some at the Junction, some on the lake bottom).
The west shore is also 'kept'. Both shores the lake said were walkable are closed.
The ship 'has passed it' and won't come back. Fair, but it confirmed I was running out of things.
Score 3 of 7. I don't know what the other four are or whether they can be reached here at all.
Drinking the invisible liquid did 'nothing unusual'. I don't know if I wasted something.

wished: Reach the south or west shore of the lake, which the lake description itself says are suitable for walking
Get past the mist toward the vegetation west of the Barren Area
Climb the endless stair once I felt 'worthy', or some way to call the old man
Some sign of what the remaining 4 points of potential are for, or where they are
Use the vial for something meaningful

lines.line: You have reached the final test, my friend! You are proved clever and powerful, but this is not yet enough! Seek me when you feel yourself worthy!
lines.why: From the arrival dream. It set my goal, and I spent the rest of the game trying to find what 'worthy' meant.

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: A good joke, and it told me the sword would come some other way.

lines.line: He has a hand cupped to one ear, turned toward the shore, as though he were waiting for somebody on it to say something to him; and the ship is not slowing down.
lines.why: A lovely nudge. It told me exactly what to do without spelling it out.

lines.line: It will take a thinner day than this one.
lines.why: A charming way to wall me off, though there were a lot of walls.

lines.line: whatever you cannot afford to lose to the bottom, your light first of all, had better be left on the shore
lines.why: A fair warning that I followed only halfway, and it cost me.

lines.line: recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded. A faint smile comes to the lips and then the face starts to change, very slowly, into that of an old, wizened person.
lines.why: The emotional high point of the game.

lines.line: The mist is empty, and it will stay empty; the ship that passes this shore has passed it.
lines.why: A beautiful line, and a door closing.

fun.why: The sailor, the dive and the hooded duel were each very satisfying. But after turn 60 it was mostly walking into 'Not today' walls and losing my items in the lake.

engagement.why: The opening dream gave me a clear purpose and I chased it hard. Once the obvious puzzles were done, I had no lead toward the 'worthy' goal, and the score of 3 of 7 just made the missing pieces more visible.

difficulty.why: The puzzles I could solve felt fair and well hinted. Losing my worn items in the lake and dying to the roc were harsh but fair enough. But the remaining points looked locked away rather than hard.

interestingness.why: Meeting my own face under the hood, the sword appearing in my hand, and the prison-cell vision when I died all gave the place a mythic feel that I wanted more of.

prose.why: The new lines are warm and wry ('a thinner day than this one', 'the south shore keeps'). The ocean description is lovely. Some replies were bare room names when I expected more.
